name: Fieschergletscher

tier.2016: extrapolated back from the 2017 survey at the cell scale of the first segment; not checked (no summer ICESat-2 shots)
tier.2017: measured: swissALTI3D 2019 edition (survey 2017), placed at 2017-09-21; not checked (no summer ICESat-2 shots)
tier.2018: interpolated between the 2017 survey, the 2021 lidar and the 2023 survey (lowering shape of the neighbouring Grosser Aletsch); not checked (no summer ICESat-2 shots)
tier.2019: interpolated between the 2017 survey, the 2021 lidar and the 2023 survey (lowering shape of the neighbouring Grosser Aletsch); not checked (no summer ICESat-2 shots)
tier.2020: interpolated between the 2017 survey, the 2021 lidar and the 2023 survey (lowering shape of the neighbouring Grosser Aletsch); checked against ICESat-2: 7 shots, rmse 1.39 m
tier.2021: interpolated; the swissSURFACE3D lidar (flown mostly 2021-10-14) sits on 88 % of the ice cells (computed) and fixes them from that day on; checked against ICESat-2: 923 shots, rmse 2.54 m
tier.2022: interpolated between the 2017 survey, the 2021 lidar and the 2023 survey (lowering shape of the neighbouring Grosser Aletsch); checked against ICESat-2: 55 shots, rmse 2.71 m
tier.2023: measured: newest swissALTI3D edition (2024 edition, aerial images 2023), placed at 2023-08-23 (the date GLAMOS gives for it); checked against ICESat-2: 220 shots, rmse 1.73 m
tier.2024: extrapolated beyond the 2023 survey at the cell scale of the last segment, from the smoothed difference of the surveys; checked against ICESat-2: 790 shots, rmse 1.64 m
tier.2025: extrapolated beyond the 2023 survey at the cell scale of the last segment, from the smoothed difference of the surveys; checked against ICESat-2: 252 shots, rmse 2.31 m
tier.2026: estimate: extrapolated like 2024-2025, with the 2026 balance estimated from the GLAMOS figure for Aletsch (Fiescher has no balance of its own): provisional; checked against ICESat-2: 136 shots, rmse 1.70 m

summary: Ice surface of each year 2016 to 2026 on the 3D strip: two swisstopo elevation models (2017, 2023), swisstopo lidar (2021) and an elevation-band lowering shape borrowed from Aletsch for the years between and beyond. A model, not a measurement, except where a survey lies.

anchors.survey: GLAMOS volume-change table (release 2025) lists this surface as source "sa3d-2023" with date_end 20179999: survey 2017, day unknown. Image strips over the strip in 2017 (swisstopo layer ch.swisstopo.lubis-bildstreifen): 2017-09-21 (SWISSIMAGE, 0.25 m) covers every ice cell (computed); no other 2017 strip lies on the ice.
anchors.placed_at: 2017-09-21 (the only 2017 strip; the fit to ICESat-2 does not separate 29 Aug, 21 Sep and 30 Sep)

anchors.source: swissSURFACE3D raster (swisstopo lidar DSM, 0.5 m, read at 20 m)
anchors.survey: GPS times of the point clouds of 25 tiles read: 21 tiles hold at least 85 % of their points on a single day (2021-10-14 on most); 4 tiles flown on several days between 2021-07-23 and 2021-10-14 are not used. The lidar sits on 88 % of the ice cells (computed).

built from aerial images 2023: strips over the ice 2023-09-05 (SWISSIMAGE, 84 % of ice cells, computed), 2023-09-06 (SWISSIMAGE, 35 %), 2023-08-22 and 2023-08-23 (CRYOSPHERE MONITORING, 7.6 % and 7.4 %); GLAMOS names 20230823 (is-stand). Which strip fed which cell is not published.
anchors.placed_at: 2023-08-23 (GLAMOS date; ICESat-2 rmse with A2 on 22 Aug, 23 Aug, 5 Sep, 6 Sep: 2.13, 2.13, 2.24, 2.25 m with A1 on 21 Sep: the fit hardly separates them; chosen on the same shots as the check, so not independent)

shape: Between two anchors the surface follows the lowering of the ice by elevation band: from snow-off (1 May plus Bw/|Bs| x 153 d, melt uniform: ASSUMPTION) to 30 September. GLAMOS release 2025 has NO balance of any kind for Fieschergletscher (the glacier list marks mass balance as not available; no row in the elevation-bin or point files). The band balance of each year is therefore that of the neighbouring Grosser Aletsch (GLAMOS release 2025, elevation bins from 1634 m, which cover the whole tongue; non-commercial). It only sets HOW the change between two surveys is spread over the years and elevations; the SIZE comes from the Fiescher surveys. Tested as donors on the same ICESat-2 shots (computed, July to October 2020-2025, one A1/A2 pair): Aletsch rmse 2.57 m, Corbassiere 2.40 m, Findel 2.47 m, Rhone 3.58 m; Aletsch scores best in 2025 (3.16 m against 3.29, 3.47 and 3.41 m), the extrapolated year. 2026 has no GLAMOS balance yet: the 2026 balance of Aletsch is estimated from the GLAMOS figure (values read from a figure, not stated numbers). Beyond the last survey (2024 to 2026) the cell scale of the last segment is kept, applied to the measured 2023 surface with its own detail from the smoothed difference of the surveys (median of 5 cells of 20 m, then a light Gaussian); the lowering fades to zero over 80 m towards the 2023 ice outline (as for Gorner, owner choice 2026-11-01). Every cell is kept between its two anchors, or beyond them within 2.5 times the lowering of its elevation band (m of ice).

validation.icesat2: ICESat-2 ATL06 v007, 2383 shots on 2023 ice, July to October, slope under 20 degrees, in 15 granules: bias 0.96 m, rmse 2.13 m over all years (error = model minus shot; the A2 day was chosen on the same shots). One shot 507 m below the surface (12 photons, snr 0.99) fails the physical envelope and is left out. Per year: 2020 1.39 m (7 shots); 2021 2.54 m (923 shots); 2022 2.71 m (55 shots); 2023 1.73 m (220 shots); 2024 1.64 m (790 shots); 2025 2.31 m (252 shots); 2026 1.70 m (136 shots). Years without summer shots are not checked.
validation.datum: Heights are corrected with a plane fitted on 5843 shots on stable ground outside the ice (NMAD 1.25 m).
validation.not_checked: The split of the loss between years is an assumption (even melt from snow-off to 30 September, band balance borrowed from Aletsch). ICESat-2 scores the surface in the years with shots, not each year step; 2016, 2018 and 2019 have no summer shots. There are no stakes: GLAMOS has no point balance for Fieschergletscher.

bed: Ice surfaces are not allowed below the bedrock: swissBEDROCK (swisstopo, 10 m; under glaciers swissALTI3D minus a modelled ice thickness, GLAMOS 2020) is the floor.
not_used: No airborne research DEMs for Fieschergletscher were searched or used. Years before 2016 are not modelled: older pictures use the 2016 surface.
licences: swisstopo open government data (swissALTI3D, swissSURFACE3D, image-strip footprints). GLAMOS balances of Aletsch and volume change: non-commercial (file headers). ICESat-2 (NASA, ATL06) and ASTER AST14DEM (NASA LP DAAC): used for checking only; the ASTER terms of use were not read. GLAMOS ice thickness release 2020 (radar beds, CC BY 4.0 per the landing page) and swissBEDROCK (swisstopo open government data): used for the ice bed checks.
caveat_2026: estimate: extrapolated like 2024-2025, with the 2026 balance estimated from the GLAMOS figure for Aletsch (Fiescher has no balance of its own): provisional; checked against ICESat-2: 136 shots, rmse 1.70 m

page.mapcap: The model area = the 3D strip (outlined in black), as set in the walkthrough. Blue: ice inside the 2023 outline, about 17.6 km² (computed, 20 m cells). Red dashed: every cell modelled as ice, including ground that was ice at the 2017 survey, about 18.5 km² (computed). The 2,383 ICESat-2 shots used for the checks are shown in the 3D viewer (last section). Pictures of years before 2016 use the 2016 surface.
page.stakeNone: no stake-year: GLAMOS has no point mass balance for Fieschergletscher (release 2025: no file of the annual, winter or intermediate sets; the glacier list marks mass balance as not available).
page.icesatSub: also fits the 2023 anchor day (not independent)
page.icesatNote: Also used to choose the 2023 anchor day, so not an independent check.
page.asterNote: For scale: each used scene has a stable-terrain NMAD of 12.0 to 12.5 m (computed) (no used scene lies within 25 days of the 2023 anchor), so differences of a few metres are within ASTER's own scatter. rms = spread of the scene values of the year. Check only, not in the fit.

notes.uncertainty: Median over the ice of 2023, red whisker the 90th percentile (computed). Calibrated on the same ICESat-2 shots (anchor value = the 2023 rmse, 1.73 m, an upper value); where a year has shots it is not below their rmse. Years without shots (2016 to 2019) carry the anchor value only, a lower bound. 2026 has none: it is an estimate and its balance was read from the GLAMOS figure for Aletsch.
notes.independent: ICESat-2 also fitted the 2023 anchor day, so it is not independent. ASTER scenes are checks only (2 of 75 scenes usable; ; usable years: 2020). There are no stakes for Fieschergletscher. Click a year for the numbers.
notes.sharing: Solid: the loss between two surveys is shared over the years by an elevation-band balance borrowed from Aletsch (GLAMOS has none for Fieschergletscher; four neighbours tested on ICESat-2, Aletsch kept). Dashed: extrapolated beyond the last survey (2026 with an estimated balance). Not used: measured years.

page.viewerText: The yearly surfaces in 3D with a year slider, the same viewer as for Aletsch. Switch on ICESat-2 shots (what the model was checked against) and hover a shot for its values; the bed and uncertainty colours are in the Colour menu. There are no stake readings for Fieschergletscher. About 8 MB, loaded when you press the button.

bed.lead: Two checks on Fieschergletscher (all computed here, not source figures; a third, repeat surveys, is impossible). The bed is the rock under the ice. "Radar bed" is the radar's own bed elevation (the survey surface minus the measured thickness, from the GLAMOS release); "model bed" is swissBEDROCK, which under glaciers is swissALTI3D minus a modelled GLAMOS ice thickness.
checks:
1 · Radar bed against model bed

At the 522 radar cells (20 m, median of the points in a cell), how far apart are the two beds?

Median −1.3 m over all cells (one survey, 2011). Spread (standard deviation) 8.5 m; 86 % are within 10 m and 99 % within 30 m.

Reading: close, but not a validation. The model bed was made from this same survey (GLAMOS 2020 model, Grab et al. 2021), and at the survey lines it is the measured bed.

2 · One survey against another

Where two surveys covered the same spot, how well do they repeat?

Cannot be checked: the GLAMOS radar data of Fieschergletscher hold a single survey (2011) in the strip, so no spot has two dates.

3 · Ground that is ice free now

Radar points where the newest swissALTI3D shows ground, not ice: the exposed ground is the bed.

41 points on 1 flight profile (2011), ice about 39 m thick:

2011
Radar bed − ground now−1.4 m (−1.9 to −0.5)
Model bed − ground now−3.3 m (−4.4 to −1.8)

Median, in brackets the middle half. 20 % of the points have the radar bed above the ground now.

bed.read:
What this supports

  • At the margins both beds lie a little below the exposed ground: the radar bed by 1.4 m, the model bed by 3.3 m (medians). The radar bed is closer to the ground than the model bed.

What it does not show

  • One profile: the 41 points lie on 1 flight profile of a single survey, so the medians rest on one line.
  • Not the deep tongue: these are margin points, about 39 m of ice; deeper ice may behave differently.
  • Not a model error band: the model's own uncertainty maps are not in the GLAMOS release, and swissBEDROCK's uncertainty band under glaciers is about 0 (not usable).
  • Not screened: lakes and debris on the exposed ground, and positions at the margin (a few metres of horizontal error).

How the ice-free points were chosen

  • In the 3D strip, at least 30 m outside the SGI2023 outline (acquired 2023, all glaciers) and at least 30 m inside the SGI2016 outline, so the model had ice there.
  • Newest swissALTI3D edition, ground slope at the point at most 20°. With up to 30°: 108 points, radar −29.6 m, model −22.3 m. With a 50 m margin: 0 points; with 100 m: 0.
